newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank says agrees to lift money mkt limits.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank says agrees to lift money mkt limits.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Tuesday that it had agreed with local large banks to renew access of non-residents to the Czech money market, which had been suspended on May 22.

"Individual banks will monitor crown loans to foreign clients, and these results will be directly at the dispostion of the CNB," a CNB statement said. The CNB limited non-resident access to the local money market last month, as part of a series of measures aimed at easing downward pressure on the crown after a wave of short-selling pushed the currency to record lows.
During the crown crisis, the CNB also raised its discount rate to 13 percent from a previous 10.5 percent, and the Lombard rate to 50 percent from 14 percent.

Eventually it cut off access to the Lombard facility as well as reaching an agreement with some local banks on cutting off non-resident access to the local money market to restrain availability of crowns. The downward pressure eventually forced the CNB to allow the crown to float freely on May 27.
On Thursday the CNB said it would once again begin allowing banks access to the short-term last resort Lombard lending facility at the 50 percent rate.

The CNB has also loosened its tight grip on market liquidity in recent days through an easing of its reverse repo rate, which has fallen from 75 percent to 31 percent. Before the crown crisis, the central bank reverse repo rate stood at 12.4 percent.
